title: Global Cloud Detection for CERES Edition 4 Using Terra and Aqua MODIS Data

venue.name: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing

abstract: The Clouds and Earth's Radiant Energy System (CERES) has been monitoring clouds and radiation since 2000 using algorithms developed before 2002 for CERES Edition 2 (Ed2) products. To improve cloud amount accuracy, CERES Edition 4 (Ed4) applies revised algorithms and input data to Terra and Aqua MODerate-resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) radiances. The Ed4 cloud mask uses 5-7 additional channels, new models for clear-sky ocean and snow/ice-surface radiances, and revised Terra MODIS calibrations. Mean Ed4 daytime and nighttime cloud amounts exceed their Ed2 counterparts by 0.035 and 0.068. Excellent consistency between average Aqua and Terra cloud fraction is found over nonpolar regions. Differences over polar regions are likely due to unresolved calibration discrepancies. Relative to Ed2, Ed4 cloud amounts agree better with those from the Cloud-Aerosol Lidar and Infrared Pathfinder Satellite Observations (CALIPSO). CALIPSO comparisons indicate that Ed4 cloud amounts are more than or as accurate as other available cloud mask systems. The Ed4 mask correctly identifies cloudy or clear areas 90%-96% of the time during daytime over nonpolar areas depending on the CALIPSO-MODIS averaging criteria. At night, the range is 88%-95%. Accuracy decreases over land. The polar day and night accuracy ranges are 90%-91% and 80%-81%, respectively. The mean Ed4 cloud fractions slightly exceed the average for seven other imager cloud masks. Remaining biases and uncertainties are mainly attributed to errors in Ed4 predicted clear-sky radiances. The resulting cloud fractions should help CERES produce a more accurate radiation budget and serve as part of a cloud property climate data record.
problem: The previous CERES Edition 2 (Ed2) cloud mask underestimated global cloud amounts and suffered from inconsistencies due to calibration differences, ancillary data issues, and the use of a limited number of spectral channels, which compromised the accuracy of climate data records.
method: To improve cloud amount accuracy, this paper describes the CERES Edition 4 cloud mask algorithm, which applies additional MODIS spectral channels, new models for clear-sky ocean and snow/ice-surface radiances, and revised Terra MODIS calibrations to more accurately distinguish cloudy from cloud-free scenes.
task: The task is to document and validate the revised CERES Edition 4 global cloud detection algorithm, which improves cloud amount accuracy by applying new methods and additional spectral channels from Terra and Aqua MODIS data.
innovation: This paper presents the revised CERES Edition 4 cloud detection algorithm, which improves cloud amount accuracy by incorporating additional MODIS spectral channels, new clear-sky radiance models, and updated calibrations to create a more accurate cloud property climate data record.

The retrieval portion of SatCORPS-CM4 is described in [15]. SatCORPS-CM4 provides the cloud property information used in the greater CERES Edition 4 processing system.

kg_extraction_triplets.paragraph: Initial comparisons with Version 2 of the CloudAerosol Lidar and Infrared Pathfinder in Space Observations (CALIPSO) [10] vertical feature mask confirmed that the Ed2 cloud mask underestimated cloud amount [11], [12].

The first operational version of the mask, Edition 2 (Ed2), was developed for application to data from the Tropical Rainfall Monitoring Mission (TRMM) Visible and InfraRed Scanner (VIRS) and the Terra and Aqua MODerate-resolution Imaging Spectroradiometers (MODIS) data. Each of those satellites carries a CERES broadband scanner. To ensure consistency among the CERES measurements from those satellites so that they could be seamlessly merged, the cloud mask was constrained, for the most part, to use spectral channels common to all three imagers: the visible (VIS, 0.64 µm), near-infrared (NIR, 1.64 µm), shortwave infrared (SIR, 3.8 µm), infrared window (IRW, 11 µm), and split-window (SPW, 12 μm) bands. A few extra channels were used in the polar regions, which were not observed by the VIRS. The Ed2 version is used for the CERES Edition 2 and 3 products [6]. The CERES Ed2 nonpolar cloud mask is detailed in [7], while [8] describes the Ed2 polar scene ID.
